title: Freya and the Archive
premise: Xanthe Pemberton, a xenolinguist whose dreams have gone silent in every human tongue, ferries messages between the colony world Vesperine and a fleet that has been at truce for nine years. When the colony's children begin sharing one identical dream — of a burning settlement and a language no human speaks — Xanthe realizes they are remembering a massacre that official archives insist never happened. As the truce deadline approaches and the fleet prepares to withdraw, she must decode the children's shared vision, find physical proof buried beneath the archive's careful erasures, and confront the archivist who falsified the record to preserve peace. She succeeds by teaching the fleet to read the dream itself as testimony, ending the silence between worlds — though it costs her the one relationship she chose over duty.
about_author: Wren Yarrow is a former radio astronomer who spent six years listening to signals nobody else believed were meaningful. They write science fiction about people who translate what others refuse to hear, and live on a coastal island with too many dictionaries.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Xanthe pilots the relay run between Vesperine and the fleet, cataloguing languages that have stopped being spoken. POV: Xanthe. Beat: loneliness established; her dreams come only in dead alien tongues now, and she has stopped telling anyone.

chapters.title: Children of One Sleep
chapters.summary: Seventeen colony children wake reciting the same unfamiliar syllables. Their teacher, Idris Okonkwo, begs Xanthe to listen. POV: Xanthe with Idris. Beat: wonder curdling into unease as she recognizes the phonemes from her own silent dreams.

chapters.title: What the Archive Says
chapters.summary: Xanthe petitions Fleet Archivist Sera Voss for records of the settlement called Halcyon Reach. Every file is pristine, complete, and wrong. POV: Xanthe. Beat: first confrontation with Voss; dread that the erasure was professional work.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through the fleet's truce negotiations, told via archived transmissions Xanthe illegally pulls. POV: alternating documents and Xanthe reading them. Beat: she sees how peace was purchased with a lie, and understands why no one wants it reopened.

chapters.title: Idris
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Idris grow close decoding the children's dream together; he lost family at Halcyon Reach and doesn't know it. POV: Idris. Beat: tenderness and found family among the children, shadowed by what the truth will cost them all.

chapters.title: The Buried Grid
chapters.summary: Following the dream's geography, Xanthe locates Halcyon Reach's actual ruins beneath an officially 'uninhabited' floodplain. POV: Xanthe. Beat: triumph turning to horror as she finds mass graves and a fleet beacon still transmitting the cover story.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: The fleet announces withdrawal in thirty days; without proof filed before departure, the massacre will be unprovable forever. Voss offers Xanthe a promotion to stay silent. POV: Xanthe. Beat: love against duty crystallizes — accepting means keeping Idris safe and the lie intact.

chapters.title: Testimony in Tongues
chapters.summary: Xanthe realizes the dream itself is evidence: the children share a xenolinguistic memory imprint from a dying survivor. She begins teaching the fleet's adjudicators to read it. POV: ensemble, anchored on Idris. Beat: fragile hope as the impossible becomes admissible.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Voss attempts to purge the children's records and quarantine the dreamers; Xanthe broadcasts the raw dream-archive fleet-wide mid-hearing. POV: Xanthe and Voss. Beat: climax — truth versus order in open conflict, and Xanthe chooses truth knowing it may break everything.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Human Again
chapters.summary: The tribunal validates the testimony; the truce is renegotiated on honest terms, and Halcyon Reach gets its names back. Xanthe and Idris part — he stays with the children, she takes the long route as their voice between worlds. POV: Xanthe. Beat: bittersweet resolution; her dreams return, finally in languages everyone can share.
